idiom_name: async trait facade + tokio oneshot correlation table
implementation_notes: Declare the contract as a trait with async methods and implement it on a struct that owns the broker client (lapin, rdkafka, a redis connection). The method-call illusion is built from two primitives: each call creates a tokio::sync::oneshot channel, stores the Sender in a map keyed by correlation id and awaits the Receiver, while the consumer task routes each reply to the waiting caller; Sender::send is not async, so the consumer can complete a call without awaiting. Nothing generates the facade - no proxies, no annotations - and a framework such as tarpc or tonic only provides a comparable client if you accept its own RPC protocol, so the manual route is the normal one.
pitfalls: The correlation table is shared mutable state: remove the entry on every exit path (reply, timeout, cancellation) or it grows for the lifetime of the process.
A dropped Sender makes the Receiver resolve with RecvError, which cannot distinguish 'timeout' from 'connection died'; keep your own deadline with tokio::time::timeout and your own error variant.
async fn in traits is not object-safe, so a dyn-dispatched gateway needs an explicitly boxed future in the signature - a design decision to make early rather than a later refactor.
Serialization errors are easy to fold into 'no reply'; a decode failure and a missing answer usually require different reactions at the call site.
